plots.name: acceptance.svg
plots.caption: Rolling acceptance rate per simulated writer. Read beside the edit-distance curve: accepting more while rewriting just as much is not improvement.

plots.name: bandit_regret.svg
plots.caption: Cumulative pseudo-regret. Thompson sampling pays its exploration cost early and then flattens; epsilon-greedy keeps paying forever.

plots.name: checker_recall.svg
plots.caption: What each checker layer contributes. Layer 1 is deterministic and free; layer 2 handles only the free-text residue it cannot decide.

plots.name: diversity_quality.svg
plots.caption: Diversity against quality on six candidates whose three best are near-paraphrases. The temperature-only baseline takes all three.

plots.name: edit_distance.svg
plots.caption: How much the writer rewrote what they took, over the run.

plots.name: mmr_lambda_sweep.svg
plots.caption: Where MMR's diversity term stops binding. At the conventional 0.7 it reproduces the baseline exactly; the DPP reaches the diverse answer with no parameter at all.

plots.name: pretraining_lift.svg
plots.caption: Whether the population prior earns its place on a writer it never saw. It helps while data is scarce and converges to irrelevance, which is the shape a prior should have.

plots.name: probe_agreement.svg
plots.caption: The deconfounded learning curve. The same frozen decisions, sampled from other writers’ runs, re-ranked by the head after every episode — so nothing in it can move because the task got harder.

plots.name: recovery_ceiling.svg
plots.caption: The ceiling on weight recovery at a given number of decisions, with the estimator correctly specified by construction. It is what makes a measured recovery readable: the same number means different things at n=20 and n=200.

plots.name: stale_precision_recall.svg
plots.caption: Staleness prediction. Declared dependency edges are exact but blind to what nobody declared; embedding edges trade precision for recall, swept by threshold.
